items.title: Drivers: hv: Don't reset VMBus connection state on error/exit paths
items.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Drivers: hv: Don't reset VMBus connection state on error/exit paths

In two places, current code forces vmbus_connection.conn_state to
DISCONNECTED prior to calling vmbus_disconnect(). But vmbus_disconnect()
calls vmbus_initiate_unload(), which unloads the VMBus connection
only if the conn_state is CONNECTED. Consequently, the connection
remains and the Hyper-V host might continue to send messages or post
VMBus interrupts.

The problem was introduced in commit 74347a99e73ae ("x86/Hyper-V:
Unload vmbus channel in hv panic callback"), in that
vmbus_initiate_unload() started checking the current connection
state before doing the unload. This commit removed some occurrences
where conn_state was forced to DISCONNECTED, but these two remained,
apparently due to an oversight at the time.

Fix this by not forcing conn_state to DISCONNECTED during VMBus exit,
or if a failure occurs when establishing the connection in the first
place. Whatever value conn_state has at the time is then read by
vmbus_initiate_unload() to determine if there is a connection to
be unloaded.

items.title: Talos Linux: Support bundle does not redact registry credentials
items.description:
### Summary
When generating a support bundle with `talosctl support` the credentials entered for private registries are included in the bundle.


### Details

Within the generated support bundle, inside `resources/registryconfigs.cri.talos.dev.yaml` the `auth` field of the spec is retained.
The same, potentially sensitive information is present within `etcfilespecs.files.talos.dev.yaml`.

### PoC

Simply run `talosctl -n [...] support` on a cluster with a `RegistryAuthConfig` resource 

### Impact

The problem itself is minor, however, anyone who has ever uploaded a support.zip bundle on a github issue, slack thread or public forum could have potentially leaked their internal authentication parameters for a private registry.

In most situations, if the network and credentials are set correctly, this should not be a problem. On the other hand, if the affected registry is publicly accessible, and the provided credentials have write access to it, this could lead to possibly serious consequences, from denial of service, to data loss and possibly existing tag hijacking leading to supply chain compromise, for the affected parties which were under the impression that the support bundle is redacted of sensitive information and thus can be shared publicly.


### Notes

Talos 1.14+ by default encrypts the support bundle to the age recipients specified (defaulting to siderolabs GitHub org members), so the impact is even lower.

### Environment

- Talos version: v1.13.0
- Kubernetes version: 1.35.3
- Platform: amd64

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.19.0 until 0.32.0, authenticated callers can supply a request chat template when no server-side --chat-template is configured, or a malicious model repository can provide a template that is compiled and rendered by tokenizer.apply_chat_template() without a wall-clock timeout, output-size limit, or iteration bound. Rendering runs in a ThreadPoolExecutor with one worker by default, so a nonterminating render can block /v1/responses and other chat-template users after the request ends, while an output-expanding render can exhaust server memory. Harmony models are not affected because they do not use this Jinja path. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder in phi4mm_audio.py and phi4mm_utils.py uses eager attention by default, allowing a remote client to submit one legal long audio clip that causes MultiHeadedAttention.forward_attention to materialize and retain full attention matrices in self.attn. The scaled dot-product attention branch does not materialize these matrices. The resulting quadratic GPU-memory use can cause an out-of-memory condition and terminate EngineCore for all users. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.11.1 until 0.32.0, the DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, and Unlimited-OCR image path allows a remote client that can reach the OpenAI-compatible API to submit a legal image whose normalized pixels sum to zero when that image is alone in its per-step encoder batch. _parse_and_validate_image_input returns no embedding, embed_multimodal propagates that value, and sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs triggers a fatal assertion that shuts down the engine for all users. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. From 0.16.0 until 0.32.0, the /v1/responses endpoint allows an authenticated caller to place an attacker-controlled template in chat_template_kwargs[chat_template] when no server template is configured. ChatParams.get_apply_chat_template_kwargs() preserves that value without enforcing trust_request_chat_template, so the request can bypass the intended trust policy and cause CPU or memory exhaustion through Jinja rendering. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

The Redis server command parser in Apache bRPC accepts an empty RESP array as a command header. A remote unauthenticated attacker who can reach a bRPC server with Redis service enabled can send an empty array header followed by a bulk string, causing an out-of-bounds write in the parser and crashing the process.

Root Cause:
RedisCommandParser::ConsumeImpl rejected negative RESP array counts but accepted zero. It resized the command argument vector to zero elements and continued parsing. When a following bulk string was parsed, the only index guard was a CHECK. In configurations where fatal logs do not abort immediately, execution could continue and write to _args[0] even though the vector was empty.

Affected Scenarios:
Deployments that enable ServerOptions.redis_service and accept Redis protocol traffic from untrusted clients. The issue is reached during parsing before command handling or authentication.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3354 

Note:
The fix rejects empty RESP arrays as invalid Redis commands and replaces the internal index CHECK with an explicit parse error so malformed command streams cannot fall through to an indexed vector write.

pghoard is a PostgreSQL backup daemon and restore tooling that stores backup data in cloud object stores. Prior to version 2.7.1, when using .pgpass, database connection information including the username and password will be logged at the debug level. This issue has been patched in version 2.7.1.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the OpenAI-compatible server configures Starlette CORSMiddleware with allowed_origins set to a wildcard by default. A malicious web page can use a victim's browser to reach an unauthenticated vLLM server on localhost, an internal network, or a VPN, call endpoints including GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions, consume GPU resources, and read responses. Cookie-based cross-site request forgery does not apply because credentials are disabled by default, and deployments requiring bearer authentication are exposed only when the caller already has a usable token. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability on 32-bit systems that allows attackers to overwrite heap memory when convex-hull information is requested. Attackers can supply crafted images processed with convex-hull calculations to corrupt heap memory, causing crashes or potential code execution.

ImageMagick before 7.1.2-33 contains a memory leak vulnerability in the magick compare command caused by missing cleanup when an operation fails. Attackers can supply inputs that trigger repeated failed compare operations to exhaust memory and cause denial of service.

ImageMagick before 6.9.13-58 and 7.x before 7.1.2-32 contains a security policy bypass caused by an incomplete fix for the policy bypass reported in GHSA-jjp4-3fwf-393j. An attacker able to supply input to ImageMagick can evade configured security policy restrictions, allowing operations the policy was intended to block.

Uncontrolled recursion in the Redis reply parser in Apache bRPC < 1.18.0 allows a remote Redis server peer to crash a bRPC Redis client process by returning a deeply nested RESP array reply. The parser recursed once for each nested array level without enforcing a depth limit. The fix adds a configurable Redis reply depth limit with default value 128 and rejects replies exceeding that limit. 

Affected Scenarios:
Applications using bRPC as a Redis client with ChannelOptions.protocol="redis" and receiving replies from an untrusted or faulty Redis server peer.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to 1.18.0.
2. Apply the patch from PR  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3344 .

Note:
After applying the fix, Redis replies with array nesting deeper than redis_max_reply_depth are rejected.

The Redis protocol implementation in Apache bRPC allowed inline command parsing to allocate and copy the full connection buffer before a complete CRLF-terminated command was available. A remote attacker with access to a Redis-protocol bRPC service could send long inline inputs without a terminating CRLF to increase memory usage and CPU copy overhead, potentially causing denial of service.


Root Cause:
The Redis inline command parser allocated memory based on the current input buffer size and copied the entire buffer before determining the current inline command boundary. The existing redis_max_allocation_size limit was applied to RESP bulk strings and arrays, but not effectively to the inline command path before allocation.


Affected Scenarios:
Use Apache bRPC server with Redis protocol enabled and reachable by untrusted clients.


How to Fix:
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply the patch from PR  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3363 .


Note:
The fix applies redis_max_allocation_size to Redis inline command lines and scans for CRLF before allocating parser arena memory. Inline command lines exceeding this limit are rejected.

items.title: Quadratic Cohere2 Vision preprocessing DoS via request-controlled max_patches
items.description:
## Summary

The Python OpenAI-compatible server accepts a request-controlled
`mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches` value when serving Cohere2 Vision models.
vLLM forwards the value to the Hugging Face processor without applying a
server-side upper bound. The processor enumerates candidate tile aspect ratios
with two loops whose bounds are both controlled by `max_patches`, causing
quadratic CPU work before normal inference limits can protect the service.

A client that can access the chat-completions endpoint can submit a small,
valid image together with a large `max_patches` value. Varying the value across
requests also avoids reuse of the helper's small LRU cache. This can occupy
multimodal preprocessing workers, substantially increase request latency, and
deny service to other clients.

No code execution, confidentiality impact, or integrity impact was
demonstrated.

## Confirmed Affected Revision

The issue was rechecked on 2026-09-08 against the then-current upstream
`main` commit:

```text
f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b
```

Commit permalink:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b

The original audited revision was:

```text
7ca49fbe4bab019e55d57cdc4b7fd3d55c67c1a6
```

The vulnerable data flow was present at the revision assessed in this report.

## Why This Is a Security Issue

`max_patches` is a computational budget, but the Python serving path lets a
remote request choose it. The expensive enumeration occurs during request
preprocessing, before the request reaches normal model execution. A small
request body can therefore trigger work disproportionate to its size.

The default server does not require an API key. If an operator configures API
authentication, exploitation instead requires a client authorized to call the
affected endpoint.

## Pre-requisites

- vLLM is serving a Cohere2 Vision model through the Python OpenAI-compatible
  frontend.
- The caller can submit an image chat request.
- The request supplies a large positive integer as
  `mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches`.

No special build flag, remote model code, malformed image, or unsafe runtime
option is required. The issue is model-specific and is not a claim that every
vLLM deployment is affected.

## Technical Details

The request-to-sink chain at the confirmed revision is:

1. `ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs` is an unrestricted
   `dict[str, Any]`:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L372-L375
2. `OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat` copies the request value into both the chat
   parameters and prompt extras:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L675-L704
3. `BaseRenderer` applies the extras and constructs `MMProcessorInputs` with
   the same processor kwargs:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/base.py#L769-L779
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/renderers/base.py#L846-L880
4. `Cohere2VisionProcessingInfo.get_num_patches` passes the merged mapping to
   `get_number_of_image_patches` without bounding `max_patches`:
   https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/f6326f53bda46898a331c2d24500332c285d9a2b/vllm/model_executor/models/cohere2_vision.py#L170-L188
5. In Transformers 5.16.1, `get_number_of_image_patches` reads
   `max_patches` from that mapping and calls `get_optimal_tiled_canvas`:
   https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.16.1/src/transformers/models/cohere2_vision/image_processing_cohere2_vision.py#L257-L285
6. The aspect-ratio helper loops from 1 through the attacker-selected value in
   both dimensions:
   https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.16.1/src/transformers/models/cohere2_vision/image_processing_cohere2_vision.py#L53-L80

The relevant operation is equivalent to:

```python
for width in range(1, max_image_tiles + 1):
    for height in range(1, max_image_tiles + 1):
        if width * height <= max_image_tiles:
            aspect_ratios.append((width, height))
```

The nested loops perform Theta(`max_patches` squared) iterations. The helper
has an LRU cache of only ten argument values, so requests using distinct large
values continue to force cold computations.

## Expected Result

Request-level processor overrides must not be able to raise a server-owned
preprocessing budget beyond a safe configured limit. An excessive value should
be rejected before invoking the Hugging Face processor.

## Security Impact

A remote or API-authorized caller can consume disproportionate CPU time in the
multimodal preprocessing path. Repeated cold computations can delay image
requests and reduce or deny availability for other clients. The demonstrated
impact is limited to availability.

## Severity Assessment

- Severity: Moderate
- CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- CVSS v3.1: 5.3
- Vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L`

`PR:N` reflects the default server configuration without an API key. An
authenticated deployment changes the required access conditions, and the vLLM
team should assign the final severity and version range.

## Duplicate Search

On 2026-09-08, public vLLM issues, pull requests, and published GitHub Security
Advisories were searched using combinations of `max_patches`, `Cohere2
Vision`, `get_all_supported_aspect_ratios`, `mm_processor_kwargs`, `quadratic`,
and `denial of service`. No public report with this specific model, request
parameter, and root cause was found.

Private vulnerability reports are not searchable, so this does not rule out a
private duplicate.

## Suggested Remediation

- Treat the server/model configuration as the authority for the maximum
  permitted patch count.
- Reject request-level `max_patches` values that are not strict positive
  integers or that exceed that server-owned limit.
- Apply the validation to both flat and modality-scoped processor kwargs where
  supported.
- Add tests proving that an oversized value is rejected before Cohere2 Vision
  preprocessing and that safe values continue to work.
- Consider improving the upstream Transformers enumeration independently, but
  do not rely on that optimization as the request-boundary security control.

## Disclosure Coordination

Please handle this report through vLLM's private vulnerability-reporting
workflow. No public issue or pull request has been created for this finding.
The reporter can provide additional source traces or help validate a proposed
fix. Public disclosure and any public remediation pull request should follow
the maintainers' triage and coordination guidance.

## Affected versions

- Package: `vllm` (PyPI).
- Affected versions: `>= 0.10.1, < 0.31.0`.
- First stable patched version: `0.31.0`.

PR #58830 blocks untrusted per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` and `media_io_kwargs` by default before preprocessing. Keep `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` disabled for untrusted clients. Explicitly enabling it restores trusted override behavior; the underlying processor/sampler is not independently bounded by this fix.

Advisory fixed in [#58830](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830).
